observation_summary: The application throws a NullPointerException when using Mockito matchers like isA(), eq(), and same() with primitive-wrapper types (e.g., Integer).
hypothesis: The matchers were incorrectly returning null instead of a default value appropriate for the type being matched, causing a NullPointerException when the framework attempted to use the returned value in a context expecting a non-null object or a specific primitive type.
prediction: The fix will change the return value of the matcher methods from a hardcoded null to a method that returns a default value based on the class type.
experiment_rationale: The diff shows that the methods isA(), eq(), and same() were changed from returning reportMatcher(...).returnNull() to reportMatcher(...).returnFor(clazz) or returnFor((Class) value.getClass()). This confirms that the root cause was an incorrect initialization/assignment of the return value.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by an incorrect return value (null) being assigned/returned by the matcher methods. The fix replaces this incorrect value with a correct one derived from the class type. This is a classic Assignment/Initialization defect where the state (the return value) was initialized incorrectly.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows the change from returnNull() to returnFor(clazz) in isA, eq, and same methods.
The failing tests indicate a NullPointerException when using these matchers.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the return value is part of a method, the core issue is the specific value being returned (null vs. a default value), which is an initialization/assignment concern rather than a procedural logic error.
